name: Scale-Split Dual-Aether Screened-Frame (SSDA-SF)
claimed_mechanism: Two timelike aether vectors are introduced with independent, constant finite kinetic normalizations (scale-split architecture). Vector A provides the off-ray preferred-frame carrier required by DC-013 to correct the MOND lensing slip, with its PPN-visible coupling strictly proportional to e^-y. Vector B is introduced to satisfy auxiliary constraint requirements, also with an e^-y screened coupling. Because both kinetic terms are bare constants, the screening of the PPN response (alpha -> 0 as y -> infinity) does not touch the propagating-mode kinetic normalization, explicitly satisfying the A3/P7 decoupling mandate.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field Newtonian limit, the e^-y screening suppresses both alpha_1 and alpha_2 exponentially, ensuring Solar System compliance (G7). The off-ray coupling from vector A generates a distinct Phi and Psi potential, breaking the f(R)-type slip of DC-013 and yielding the correct MOND-enhanced lensing (G6). Because the kinetic coefficients are finite and independent of the screened couplings, the theory remains weakly coupled in the high-acceleration regime (G8), avoiding the strong-coupling wall that killed the khronometric and single-aether architectures.
inequivalence_argument: This architecture is structurally inequivalent to the killed khronometric MOND (DC-010), which relied on a single khronon field whose c_s^2 was tightly coupled to the screening function, causing a P7 strong-coupling wall. It differs from AeST (DC-002) because the preferred-frame couplings are explicitly e^-y screened rather than constant, avoiding the alpha_2 ~ 1/K_B PPN kill. The dual-vector, scale-split design with independently normalized kinematics provides a mathematically distinct route to the P7-decoupled preferred frame that has not been previously evaluated.
